examples.problem_statement: Find the value of 6 + 4 ÷ (5 − 3)

solution.description: According to PEMDAS/BODMAS, we must solve operations inside parentheses first
Next, we perform division before addition as per order of operations
Finally, we perform the addition operation

examples.problem_statement: Determine the value of 13 − 2 × 3 + 14 ÷ (2 + 5)

solution.description: Brackets come first in BODMAS, so evaluate 2 + 5 = 7 and rewrite the expression with 14 divided by 7 in place of the bracket.
Division outranks addition and subtraction, so carry out 14 divided by 7 and replace it with 2.
Multiplication is the remaining higher-precedence operation: 2 times 3 is 6, leaving 13 - 6 + 2.
Only addition and subtraction are left and they rank equally, so collect the two positive terms: 13 + 2 gives 15, leaving 15 - 6.
Finish with the single subtraction that remains: 15 - 6 = 9.
Work outward from the innermost bracket: 4 times 6 is 24, so the square bracket becomes 3 + 24 - 21.
Close both remaining brackets: 3 + 24 - 21 is 6, and 2 + 6 is 8, so the expression is now 16 divided by 8 plus 18 times 6, since a number written against a bracket multiplies it.
Do the division: 16 divided by 8 is 2, leaving 2 plus 18 times 6.
Multiplication still outranks addition, so evaluate 18 times 6 as 108 before touching the plus sign.
Add the two remaining terms: 2 + 108 = 110.

examples.problem_statement: Find the value of 23 − 4(2 × 7) + \frac{144 \div 4}{14 - 8}

solution.description: Clear the grouped parts first: the bracket 2 times 7 is 14, and the fraction bar groups its own numerator and denominator, so 144 divided by 4 is 36 over 14 - 8 = 6.
The fraction is now a plain division, so 36 over 6 becomes 6.
Multiplication comes before addition and subtraction: the 4 sitting against the bracket multiplies 14 to give 56.
Addition and subtraction rank equally, so gather the two positive terms, 23 + 6 = 29, leaving 29 - 56.
Subtracting the larger number from the smaller gives a negative answer: 29 - 56 = -27.

examples.problem_statement: Evaluate \frac{3 + \sqrt{(5^2 - 3^2)} + 2^3}{1 + (4 \times 6) \div (3 \times 4)} + \frac{15 \div 3 + 2 \times 7 - 1}{3 \times \sqrt{4} + 8 - 3^2 + 1}

solution.description: Deal with every power, root and bracket first: 5 squared minus 3 squared is 16 whose square root is 4, 2 cubed is 8, 4 times 6 is 24, 3 times 4 is 12, 15 divided by 3 is 5, the square root of 4 is 2, and 3 squared is 9.
Next in order come the divisions and multiplications left inside each fraction: 24 divided by 12 is 2, and 2 times 7 is 14.
Now add and subtract within each numerator and each denominator, since the fraction bar groups them: 3 + 4 + 8 is 15 over 1 + 2 = 3, and 5 + 14 - 1 is 18 over 6 + 8 - 9 + 1 = 6.
Carry out the two divisions the fraction bars now stand for: 15 over 3 is 5, and 18 over 6 is 3.
Add the two simplified fractions to finish: 5 + 3 = 8.

key_reminders: {'point': 'The order of precedence of operations is remembered by the word BODMAS.'}
{'point': 'Note that a number outside of a bracket multiplies all that is inside the brackets.'}

Forgetting that a fraction bar groups its numerator and denominator, so 144 divided by 4 over 14 - 8 gets read as 144 divided by 4 divided by 14, minus 8.

examples.problem_statement: In Figure 21.3, find the length of EF

solution.description: From the problem statement and figure, we know the hypotenuse e and one side f of the right triangle.
In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of the other two sides.
Plug in the known values for e and f.
Work out the two squares: 13 times 13 is 169 and 5 times 5 is 25, so the relation reads 169 = d squared + 25.
Subtract 25 from both sides to leave d squared on its own, giving 169 - 25 = 144.
Take the positive square root of 144, since a length cannot be negative, which gives d = 12.
Attach the unit carried by the given lengths and report the answer: EF, the side labelled d, is 12 cm.

examples.problem_statement: Two aircraft leave an airfield at the same time. One travels due north at an average speed of 300km/h and the other due west at an average speed of 220km/h. Calculate their distance apart after 4 hours

solution.operation: After 4 hours, the first aircraft has travelled $4 \times 300 = 1200\text{km}$ due north
solution.description: Distance is speed multiplied by time, so in 4 hours the northbound aircraft covers 4 times 300 = 1200 km.

solution.operation: and the second aircraft has travelled $4 \times 220 = 880\text{km}$ due west
solution.description: Apply the same speed times time calculation to the westbound aircraft: 4 times 220 = 880 km.

North and west are at right angles to one another, so the two flight paths and the gap between the aircraft form a right triangle with that gap, BC, as the hypotenuse; Pythagoras therefore gives BC squared as the sum of the two squares.
Square each distance and add them: 1200 squared is 1440000, 880 squared is 774400, and together they make 2214400.
Take the square root of 2214400 to turn BC squared back into a length, giving the separation as 1488 km.
